title: ops availability sprint playbook for customer impact scenarios
summary: A practical, cross-functional 6-week sprint plan to operationalize availability SLOs, validate instrumentation, and run customer-impact rehearsals. Focus: reduce noisy alerts, establish rollback policies, and align product+SRE on remediation playbooks.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a hands-on 6-week activation sprint to move availability SLOs from design into practice across product teams, SRE, and platform. Goal is not perfection — iterate quickly: prove instrumentation, calibrate thresholds on production-like traffic, and create a clear escalation/rollback path for customer-impact incidents.

Context / Why now:
- Recent incidents exposed unclear ownership for degraded inference tail latency and fallback behavior across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Teams have SLO drafts but missing: test traffic profiles, alert tuning, and documented customer-impact exercises.
- Executive ask: demonstrable reduction in P1/SEV1 pages over next quarter and concrete oncall playbooks for model-serving endpoints.

Scope (what this sprint covers):
- Services: api-proxy, inference-router, kv-cache, batching-service, fleeter (GPU pool manager)
- Telemetry: request latency p50/p90/p99, per-route error-rate, cache-hit-rate, queue-depth, GPU-utilization, cold-start counts
- Out of scope: billing pipeline, long-term cost-optimizations (handled by Optimize backlog)

Sprint length: 6 weeks (recommended cadence)
- Week 0 (prep): finalize participants, map dependencies, baseline metrics
- Weeks 1–4 (iterative work): instrumentation fixes, alert tuning, tabletop drills, small production trials
- Week 5 (customer-impact rehearsal): orchestrated degraded-mode test on canary, verify fallbacks and SLIs
- Week 6 (retro + handoff): update runbooks, accept criteria, plan next 90-day improvements

Primary stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Project lead: Lena Park (platform-engineering) — coordinate cross-team calendar, decisions, exec updates
- SRE lead: Marco Alvarez — alerting, oncall choreography, runbook edits
- Product owner (model-serving): Sasha Patel — define customer-impact scenarios & acceptance criteria
- Observability engineer: Ethan Li — dashboards, synthetic traffic harness, tracing correlation
- Solutions/SE: Priya Nair — customer expectations, canary scheduling for enterprise tenants

Ownership matrix (quick reference):
- Alert triage + first-response: SRE oncall (Marco's rota)
- Escalate to platform triage: platform-engineering pager
- Model fallback policy changes: product + applied-ml review
- Communication (customers/CS): solutions engineering -> CS lead

Deliverables by end of sprint:
- Verified SLI definitions and baseline metrics for each service (documented in Confluence)
- Adjusted alert thresholds to target actionable signals only (reduce noise by >=30% target)
- A concrete rollback and degraded-mode playbook for each major route (text runbook + checklist)
- A canary run that simulates a GPU pool degradation for a low-volume tenant and a postmortem-style report
- Updated oncall runbooks and handoff doc for product teams

Key milestones and success criteria:
- M1 (end Week 1): baseline dashboards and synthetic traffic harness available; list of instrumentation gaps identified
- M2 (end Week 3): 75% of instrumentation gaps closed or tracked with PRs; initial alert tuning applied on staging
- M3 (end Week 5): Canary exercise executed; fallbacks triggered successfully for control tenant; incident timeline and decision log recorded
- Acceptance: No new P1 drops attributable to the tested failure modes for 2-week observation post-canary.

Tactical checklist (what to do, short bullets):
- Inventory: export current alerts for services -> categorize noisy vs actionable
- Instrumentation: add p99 histograms for routing latency and KV cache miss tags
- Tracing: ensure trace ids flow across api-proxy -> router -> model-host; add sampling rules for high-cardinality keys
- Synthetic tests: build 3 traffic profiles (baseline, spike, tail-heavier) and run nightly against staging
- Alert rules: make alerts multi-window (e.g., p99 over 5m AND error-rate above threshold) to reduce flapping
- Fallbacks: codify fallback policy decision table (when to return cached summary vs degrade model size)
- Canary run: schedule a 2-hour slot with Product + SRE; pre-notify affected customers if any

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync (30m) — Tue 09:30am PT — cadence: progress, blockers, escalations
- Incident comms template: short timeline, impact, mitigation, next steps — prefilled before canary
- Slack channel: #ops-availability-sprint (use for real-time signal during canary)
- Customer comms: Solutions will prepare a one-paragraph advisory for CS to use if customer tenants are affected

Instrumentation and tooling integration notes:
- Metrics: Prometheus + Cortex backend; ensure stable label cardinality (drop model-instance label for aggregated SLOs)
- Traces: Jaeger collector with gRPC forwarding; correlate with request_id header set by api-proxy
- Dashboards: New folder 'ops-availability-sprint' in Grafana — panels for p99 latency, error rate per route, queue depth by handler
- Synthetic harness: reuse existing harness repo (linked_artifacts: PR 412) — add new profile and runner job in CI for nightly baseline

Runbooks / Playbook snippets (to copy into oncall runbook):
- Trigger: p99 latency > 600ms for two consecutive 5m windows AND error rate > 0.5%
  - Triage steps: check GPU pool health, cache-hit-rate, and queue-depth panels
  - Quick mitigation: switch route to low-latency model variant (if configured) and increase batching window for non-realtime calls
  - Escalate to SRE lead if mitigation fails after 10 minutes
- Rollback: revert route change or model-pin via feature-flag; document time and reason in incident log

Risk register (top 5):
- Risk: Canary triggers customer impact beyond planned scope
  - Mitigation: pick low-volume control tenant, pre-announce maintenance window, have immediate rollback plan
- Risk: Alerts suppressed too aggressively -> miss real incidents
  - Mitigation: pair tuning with a small oncall squad that will monitor silently for 48 hours post-change
- Risk: High-cardinality labels increase Cortex cost
  - Mitigation: audit labels; create cardinality budget and enforce via CI linter

Open questions / decisions needed this week:
- Do we agree on the p99 threshold for inference-router for service-class B? (Product and SRE to sign off)
- Which tenant(s) are safe for canary degraded-mode? Need Solutions input.

Quick TODOs (owner):
- Lena: finalize roster and calendar by 2026-03-05
- Ethan: create synthetic profiles and wire to nightly job (due 2026-03-12)
- Marco: export alert list and propose candidate rules for noise reduction (due 2026-03-09)
- Sasha: publish customer-impact acceptance criteria doc (due 2026-03-08)

Notes / raw thoughts (working doc style):
- try to avoid renaming existing metrics in prod; cheaper to add derived panels at Grafana layer
- keep experiment small: prove one failure mode end-to-end rather than many half-baked ones
- consider adding a "degraded-mode label" to traces so we can query which traces experienced fallback logic

Post-sprint handoff (what gets put into steady state):
- Consolidated runbook in /confluence/ops/runbooks/service-availability (link to be filled)
- One-page executive summary with metrics (pre/post noisy-alert counts, canary outcomes)
- Backlog tickets for longer-term items: cardinality cleanup, batching improvements, persistent synthetic coverage

Appendix: quick checklist for the canary window
- Pre-canary: confirm synthetic baseline, notify CS, ensure rollback button is functional
- During: one SRE oncall + platform engineer in channel, product PM present, solutions on standby
- Post: 2h quiet observation, 24h elevated monitoring, and full write-up within 48h

If anything here looks off or missing, flag it in the doc comments. This is intentionally pragmatic — we want to ship a small, observable win and iterate.
